raw.assessment: The incumbent already provides usable course sets in 32/40 exports, and unchanged-assignment centers have a seven-minute median: evidence against assuming a universal workflow failure. Assignment changes and renames concentrate the observed exceptions but do not establish causes. D1-O5 limits a computation-speed explanation: replacement waits greatly exceed job duration. Zero sampled cross-center rows does not establish isolation, especially with the split-course center absent. Spreadsheet actions and timetable accuracy remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a requested historical week may exclude intended courses after reassignment.
openings.delta: Test requested-week membership before changing export scheduling or generation speed.
openings.prediction: With attendance and course identity fixed, changing only the current assignment changes incumbent historical-week membership; an explicit week-specific selection restores the expected courses.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare unchanged, midweek-reassigned, and postweek-reassigned courses against a stipulated expected set. Prototype authorized, center-scoped week selection only if the mismatch reproduces. Retain the CSV schema; test concurrent attendance entry and same-named courses across centers. Bound work to six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Assignment affects export membership, not merely displayed information.
Week-specific membership can be recovered or explicitly selected within the available budget; otherwise the prototype remains diagnostic.

openings.claim: Do renamed courses produce missing participant rows, or complete files that coordinators mistake for omissions when matching timetable names?
openings.delta: Distinguishes data omission from recognition and reconciliation work requiring different remedies.
openings.prediction: If recognition drives the rename exceptions, fabricated rows remain complete and an internal old-name/new-name mapping reduces false omission reports; true missing rows persist despite that mapping.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators in two short sessions with fabricated renamed-course exports: inspect completeness against known course identities, then compare matching and import actions with and without a private name mapping. Record checking, correction, download, and import time separately; preserve the documented CSV.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate the relevant reconciliation behavior.
A name mapping can be shown inside authorized workspaces within the shared six-day budget.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames concentrate the observed difficulties, but do not establish why files are judged incomplete. Distinguish genuine omissions from identity confusion before selecting a bounded change. The sample establishes neither isolation for split courses nor the causes of handling time.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignment to select a requested week's courses may make historical exports change after reassignment. Selecting through center-scoped course identity and assignment effective dates could prevent those omissions.
openings.delta: Treat a weekly export as a historical query whose course membership should remain stable across subsequent instructor changes.
openings.prediction: For fabricated attendance held fixed, reassigning an instructor changes the incumbent export's course set; effective-date selection restores the coordinator-confirmed set.
openings.probe: Replay one fabricated week before and after instructor reassignment, holding center, course identities and attendance constant. Compare expected course membership and CSV rows. If reproduced, estimate the smallest effective-date correction and verify unchanged schema, uninterrupted attendance entry and center isolation before committing the six-day budget.
assumptions: Course selection actually depends on instructor assignment.
Adequate assignment history exists or a bounded correction is feasible within six engineer-days and current hosting.

openings.claim: Are renamed courses present but unrecognized when coordinators compare exported names against older local timetables?
openings.delta: Test whether some replacement requests reflect identity confusion rather than absent attendance. A private old-name-to-current-name receipt could then reduce checking without changing the CSV.
openings.prediction: Affected rows remain present under the new name, and a rename receipt reduces false missing-course reports while preserving detection of a deliberately omitted course.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' sessions for counterbalanced fabricated timetable/CSV comparisons with and without a rename receipt, including an omitted-course control. Record checking time, false alarms and missed omissions inside the private service or authorized workspace. Advance only if benefit and implementation effort justify the bounded change.
assumptions: Renames preserve a recoverable course identity.
A rename receipt is not evidence that course splits or cross-center isolation are correct.

openings.claim: Current assignments may alter historical-week course membership; effective-date selection or explicit authorized week selection could restore it.
openings.discriminator: With attendance and identities fixed, does reassignment change the requested-week set?
openings.fit: Conditional: private center scope, documented CSV, concurrent attendance, six engineer-days and existing hosting.
openings.probe: Replay unchanged, midweek and postweek assignments against expected sets; test same-named courses across centers. If reproduced, estimate effective-date correction or explicit week selection.
openings.uncertainty: Selection dependency and recoverable history are unknown; explicit selection feasibility is also unproven. Otherwise remain diagnostic.

openings.claim: Renamed courses may be present but unrecognized against older timetables; a private rename mapping could reduce false omissions.
openings.discriminator: Complete renamed rows versus true missing rows; mapping must preserve omission detection.
openings.fit: Preserve private workspace, CSV and attendance access; implementation must share the six-day and hosting budget.
openings.probe: Six coordinators, two short sessions: counterbalance fabricated comparisons with/without mapping and an omitted-course control. Measure false alarms, missed omissions, checking, correction, download and import time.
openings.uncertainty: Recoverable identities, timetable accuracy and task realism remain unknown; mapping does not validate splits or isolation.

lineage.reason: With A1; retain explicit selection and reassignment timing.
With Z1; retain effective dates and history feasibility.
With A2; retain row completeness and handling components.
With Z2; retain counterbalancing and omission control.

post_distill.decision: Probe before choosing a change; correlation establishes no cause. Seven-minute stable-course handling limits universal-workflow claims; replacement waits exceed computation. Split-course isolation remains untested. Success requires next 40 exports: median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended sets, zero cross-center records.
